data.reasoning: The package is a standard AUR binary package that downloads a tarball from the official GitHub releases page (https://github.com/denix666/pax/releases/download/v${pkgver}/pax_linux_x86_64.tar.gz) with a pinned SHA256 checksum. The PKGBUILD contains only standard variable assignments and a package() function that installs the binary and generates shell completions by invoking the binary itself (a recognized pattern for prebuilt binaries). No malicious code injection, no execution of fetched content, no fetching from unrelated hosts. The single valid report (deepseek) correctly identified this as safe.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool error in the qwen model (HTTP 400 BadRequestError) when reviewing the PKGBUILD file, resulting in an 'inconclusive' verdict. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all files and found the package to be safe. The openrouter/free report was advisory-only (advisory: true) and does not count as a vote. There is no genuine disagreement about the package's safety; the inconclusive result was due to a technical failure, not uncertainty about the code.
coverage_issues: qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507: PKGBUILD review failed with HTTP 400 BadRequestError, resulting in no verdict for the most critical file
learnings: Tool errors (API failures, timeouts) should be clearly distinguished from genuine uncertainty in the verdict. An 'inconclusive' due to a tool error should not be treated the same as an 'inconclusive' due to ambiguous code.

When a critical file review fails due to a tool error, the audit tool should either retry with a different model or clearly flag the failure as a coverage issue rather than marking the entire package as inconclusive.
